title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction & spillover heuristics v18 (memory compaction + scheduling)
author: Marisol Chen
commit_summary: tune: add adaptive compaction policy and thresholds (compaction.rs)
feat: implement spillover-priority queue + background compaction task (spillover.rs, scheduler.rs)
perf: reduce fragmentation accounting overhead; switch to bucketed free lists (kv_alloc.rs)
test: add regression and integration tests for eviction under high-concurrency workloads
description:
Context & motivation:
As more request patterns exercise long-running chat sessions, we see KV cache fragmentation and paging-induced spillover becoming dominant contributors to increased GPU memory variance and tail latency. This PR implements the next iteration (v18) of adaptive eviction and spillover heuristics to reduce fragmentation, prioritize compacting hot ranges, and defer expensive compaction work to a background scheduler when possible.

What changed (single-summary):
- Adaptive compaction: new compaction policy that runs lightweight sampling to detect fragmented segments and triggers in-place compaction only when expected reclaim > config threshold. This reduces unnecessary compaction work and CPU/GPU jitter.
- Spillover priority queue: spillover now ranks candidates by estimated reuse score (recency * token-weight) to prefer evicting cold keys that save the most memory without hurting hit-rate.
- Bucketed free lists & lightweight accounting: replaced per-allocation accounting with bucketed free lists to reduce bookkeeping overhead and fragmentation amplification.
- Background compaction scheduler: compaction and coarse defragmentation are now scheduled by a background worker with configurable backpressure knobs (max concurrent compactions, cpu/gpu limit).
- Configuration: new flags and runtime knobs (kv.compaction.threshold, kv.spillover.priority_weight, kv.scheduler.max_background_compactions).
- Observability: new metrics (kv.compaction_runs, kv.compaction_reclaimed_tokens, kv.spillover_evicted_keys, kv.fragmentation_ratio) and dashboard docs updated.

Benchmarks & safety:
- Microbenchmarks: end-to-end bench shows 8-12% reduction in steady-state GPU memory footprint on long-chat workload (seq len 2048) and 4-7% improvement in p99 tail latency under high concurrency (1000 qps) when compared with v17 heuristics.
- Integration tests: added deterministic eviction tests and a stress test that validates no data races when background compaction runs concurrently with KV reads/writes.
- Rollout plan: feature gated behind kv.compaction.enabled and opt-in config at Dedicated/Private; default on for hosted after gradual canary.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc + heuristics discussion (link: https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-4521/kv-cache-v18-adaptive-eviction-design)
- [x] Unit tests covering compaction and spillover logic
- [x] Integration stress tests added
- [x] Benchmarks added and perf numbers recorded
- [x] Observability dashboards updated

Review notes & tradeoffs:
- We intentionally make compaction conservative to avoid introducing CPU/GPU jitter; worst-case reclaim is limited by threshold to avoid long pause.
- The spillover ranking uses an approximate reuse score to keep compute cheap; we may iterate to add memoized reuse estimates if needed.
- Bucketed free lists trade slightly coarser allocation granularity for dramatically reduced allocation overhead and lower fragmentation in practice.

Review conversation (high-level):
- Avi: "Can you add a safety valve so compaction won't trigger during critical-low-memory paths?"
- Author: "Added kv.scheduler.max_background_compactions and a runtime check to block compaction if system memory pressure > 85%. See compaction.rs:line ~210."
- Sofia: "Is the spillover ordering stable under retries? Could we see thrashing?"
- Author: "We added a decay factor in the score and a short hold window to avoid immediate re-inserts; integration test 'eviction_hold_window' covers this path."
- Jonah: "Add more visibility to the reclaim estimator so SREs can tune thresholds."
- Author: "Exposed kv.compaction.reclaim_estimate and kv.compaction.last_run_reclaimed in metrics and docs updated."

CI summary:
- presubmit/unit-tests: pass
- presubmit/integration-tests: one flaky failure on first run (timeout on stress test) — rerun passed
- perf/bench: bench_spillover shows consistent improvements vs v17 in 10/12 runs
- lint/format: pass

Merge outcome:
Squash-merged to main after approvals from Avi and Sofia. No migration or customer-facing breaking changes. Default config remains conservative.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-4603: telemetry alert thresholds for kv.fragmentation_ratio (follow-up to tune for production)
- Investigate memoized reuse estimator (future work)

This PR is focused on reducing memory variance and lowering tail latency caused by inefficient KV cache eviction and spillover. If you need help reproducing the benchmarks I can share the bench harness & raw outputs.
